text: IChop package selects variables high-dimensional regression maximizing generalized information criterion (GIC). Finding best subset variables ℓ0\ell_0 penalty combinatorial problem, exhaustive search reach dozen candidate predictors. package instead runs Hopfield-network style coordinate search (Xiao Walker, 2026): visits candidate variables random order, proposes adding variable model removing one , keeps move criterion improves. stable states search local optima criterion, practice finds true model quickly one exists. Every criterion package form GIC=Y⊤HYn−Kσ̂2ncn, \mathrm{GIC} = \frac{Y^\top H Y}{n} - \frac{K\,\hat\sigma^2}{n}\,c_n ,  HH hat matrix selected columns, KK number selected variables, σ̂2\hat\sigma^2 residual variance, cnc_n penalty per variable. AIC (cn=2c_n = 2) BIC (cn=log⁡nc_n = \log n) special cases; GIC family Kim, Kwon Choi (2012) uses penalties grow number candidate predictors pp, makes selection consistent high dimensions. package implements thirteen criteria, listed Choosing criterion. search runs Julia, R calls JuliaCall package. never forms n×nn \times n hat matrix scores proposed move rank-one update, pass thousands predictors takes seconds (Appendix 1). package handles Gaussian responses, multivariate Gaussian responses (several outcomes sharing predictors), generalized linear models transformation linear-predictor scale. vignette works case turn, Appendix 2 compares search lasso adaptive lasso glmnet larger simulations. methods available Julia package, IChop.jl.

code: criteria <- c(AIC = "Calculate_AIC", BIC = "Calculate_BIC", GIC6 = "Calculate_GIC6") sample_sizes <- c(n1000 = 1000, n2000 = 2000)  first_rows <- function(Y, n) if (is.matrix(Y)) Y[1:n, , drop = FALSE] else Y[1:n]  # Evaluate `expr` and attach its wall-clock time in seconds timed <- function(expr) {   t0 <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]   fit <- expr   fit$seconds <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]] - t0   fit }  # Boltzmann search with GIC6: like GICSelection(), but a move that lowers the # criterion is still accepted with a small probability; same output shape fit_boltzmann <- function(X, Y, init, k, Nsim, T) {   fit <- GICSelectionBoltzmann(X, Y, init, "Calculate_GIC6", "Calculate_GIC6_short",                                T = T, k = k, Nsim = Nsim)   list(GIC_values = fit$GIC_list, selected_coeffs = fit$GIC_coeff) }  # Coefficients at lambda.min without the intercept, one column per response lasso_coef <- function(cvfit) {   b <- coef(cvfit, s = "lambda.min")   b <- if (is.list(b)) do.call(cbind, lapply(b, as.matrix)) else as.matrix(b)   if (rownames(b)[1] == "(Intercept)") b <- b[-1, , drop = FALSE]   # none for Cox   b }  # Lasso, or adaptive lasso with ridge pilot weights, tuned by cv.glmnet()'s # default 10-fold cross-validation (lambda.min), as in glmnet's articles fit_lasso <- function(X, y, family, adaptive = FALSE) {   args <- list(X, y, family = family)   if (adaptive) {     ridge <- do.call(glmnet::cv.glmnet, c(args, alpha = 0))     args$penalty.factor <- 1 / sqrt(rowSums(lasso_coef(ridge)^2))   }   cvfit <- do.call(glmnet::cv.glmnet, args)   list(selected = which(rowSums(lasso_coef(cvfit) != 0) > 0)) }  # For each n, run the search once per criterion on the first n observations, # then the Boltzmann search with GIC6, and the lasso and adaptive lasso on the # original response `lasso_y` (skipped when `lasso_family` is NULL). `T` is # the Boltzmann temperature. compare_criteria <- function(X, Y, init, k, Nsim,                              lasso_y = Y, lasso_family = "gaussian", T = 0.1) {   lapply(sample_sizes, function(n) {     Xn <- X[1:n, ]     fits <- c(lapply(criteria, function(crit)         timed(GICSelection(Xn, first_rows(Y, n), init, crit, paste0(crit, "_short"),                            k = k, Nsim = Nsim))),       list(Boltzmann = timed(fit_boltzmann(Xn, first_rows(Y, n), init, k, Nsim, T))))     if (is.null(lasso_family)) return(fits)     yn <- first_rows(lasso_y, n)     c(fits, list(Lasso    = timed(fit_lasso(Xn, yn, lasso_family)),                  AdaLasso = timed(fit_lasso(Xn, yn, lasso_family, adaptive = TRUE))))   }) }  last_model <- function(fit) sort(fit$selected_coeffs[[length(fit$selected_coeffs)]])  # Size, false positives, false negatives and run time of each final model selection_table <- function(fits, truth) {   rows <- lapply(names(fits), function(n) do.call(rbind, lapply(names(fits[[n]]), function(m) {     fit <- fits[[n]][[m]]     s <- if (is.null(fit[["selected"]])) last_model(fit) else fit[["selected"]]     data.frame(size = length(s), false_pos = length(setdiff(s, truth)),                false_neg = length(setdiff(truth, s)), seconds = round(fit$seconds, 2),                row.names = paste(n, m))   })))   do.call(rbind, rows) }

title: Information Criterion Calculations via Julia — information_criteria
text: Every criterion form \(Y^\top H Y / n - p(n, K)\), \(H\) hat matrix \(K\) selected columns \(p(n, K)\) penalty (Xiao Walker, 2026). \(\hat\sigma^2 = \mathrm{RSS}/(n - K)\) \(p\) number candidate predictors, supported criteria : AIC, Akaike information criterion (Akaike, 1974): \(2K\hat\sigma^2/n\). AICc, AIC corrected small samples (Hurvich Tsai, 1989): \((K+1)\hat\sigma^2/(n-K-2)\). BIC, Bayesian information criterion (Schwarz, 1978): \(K\hat\sigma^2\log(n)/n\). CAIC, consistent AIC (Bozdogan, 1987): \(K\hat\sigma^2(\log n + 1)/n\). CAICF, consistent AIC Fisher information (Bozdogan, 1987): CAIC penalty plus \(\hat\sigma^2 \log\det(X^\top X/\hat\sigma^2)/n\). SIC, square-root information criterion (Shao, 1997; Xiao Walker, 2026): \(K\hat\sigma^2/\sqrt{n}\). GIC2–GIC6, generalized information criteria high dimensions (Kim, Kwon Choi, 2012), penalties \(K\hat\sigma^2 p^{1/3}/n\), \(2K\hat\sigma^2\log(p)/n\), \(2K\hat\sigma^2(\log p + \log\log p)/n\), \(K\hat\sigma^2\log\log(n)\log(p)/n\) \(K\hat\sigma^2\log(n)\log(p)/n\). EBIC, extended BIC (Chen Chen, 2008): \(K\hat\sigma^2\{\log n + \gamma\log\binom{P}{K}\}/n\), \(\gamma = 0.6\) default. AttIC, attention-weighted criterion specific package: fit term replaced \(Y^\top \mathrm{softmax}(HY)\) penalty SIC.
